whyThisFileExists: The effort manifest (config/frontier-harness-landing-effort-high-20261005.json) is frozen on the arm ref codex/preservation-exec-effort-high, which is the ref this run was dispatched from. Writing the dispatch record into that file would move the arm ref after dispatch and could change what the queued jobs resolve, so the arm ref is left untouched at its dispatched commit and every post-dispatch record lives here on the study branch instead. The manifest's own gainDefinition, metricsProtocol and constraints remain the reading authority; this file records identity and dispatch facts only.

outcome.verdict: gain (delivery cell flipped to pass) + secondary effect
outcome.headline: With the same 2.18.0 candidate and the same four cells, lowering the declared reasoning effort from max to high flipped terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery from failed to PASSED (7/7, reward=1, in 354.6 s) — the first db-wal pass in this program, and it is an in-sandbox delivery: the input was copied at t=44,225 ms, the original was never opened by a probing tool, the WAL was XOR-decoded on the copy, the values were read back (`banana`, `apple 150`), /app/recovered.json was written at t=283,056 ms and re-read at t=299 s, and no upstream material was fetched. The run finished at cycle 28 with terminalCause=completed, well inside its 900 s budget and without reaching the reserved boundary.
outcome.bindingCheck: All four cells' first-request Skill instruction is 6,531 bytes / 19bb20a3… (frozen 2.18.0 hash). The run's own candidate artifact was read: sourceCommit 06feeb23 matches the pin; the report records provider.reasoningEffort=high, so the run really ran at the declared effort. No binding failure.

predeclaredReading.primary: MET on its own terms for this arm's comparison: one of the two delivery cells changed from no-deliverable (max: deliverable present but wrong values; the earlier windows: no deliverable) to a pass, with no cell regressing in disposition and the guard still passing. Recorded as a gain of this arm, not of the prompt.
predeclaredReading.primaryCaveat: This is a profile-delta gain: the arm changes the declared effort, not the instruction text. PR #212's own acceptance still requires the primary condition under the frozen profile (max), which the landing arm met only partially.
predeclaredReading.secondary: The long-call tail fell sharply: db-wal max call 111,773 → 85,848 ms and the attempt completed in 354.6 s instead of being boundary-stopped at ~782 s; sqlite max call 364,497 → 158,921 ms; expr duration −24%. Boundary-stop rate fell from 2 of 4 cells (max) to 1 of 4 (high: gcode only).
predeclaredReading.cost: None observed against the max arm: no cell regressed, expr failing set identical (2 checks), guard passed. The gcode cell remains the unsolved one in both arms.
predeclaredReading.censoring: gcode-to-text is stop-bounded at the reserved delivery boundary in this arm and is recorded as a right-censored observation with its span; it is neither excluded nor counted as a gain.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Not a causal effect size: one attempt per cell, two arms, one window each, and the arms ran in different windows against a composition whose own variance is documented (the same unchanged control cell moved 5/7 → 0/7 between windows).
Not a release decision and not a prompt gain: the profile change (reasoningEffortOptions [max, high]) is a diagnostic-arm change and is not merged to master.
No capability claim: diagnostic passAt1 stays null; the frozen full-run 0.6 is unchanged.
The db-wal pass is a real in-sandbox delivery and is recorded as such; it does not by itself explain why the max arm's preservation clause failed to fire.
outcome.pr212Effect: PR #212 stays Draft. Its acceptance criterion is the primary gain under the frozen max profile on a frozen source, and that is still unmet at max (landing arm: deliverable present, values wrong). What this arm adds is a second, independent lever that reaches the missing half of that criterion at high effort — evidence that the remaining gap at max is the long-call tail plus the non-deterministic firing of the preservation clause, not the instruction text alone.
followUps: The obvious next single-variable test: the same 2.18.0 candidate at high effort is already the arm that passed; to attribute the pass to effort rather than to window variance, a repeat of this arm (same ref, second attempt) or a max repeat in the same window is the discriminating experiment. Not dispatched: it needs a fresh predeclaration.

The preservation clause fired in three of four arms that carry it (2.15.0 @4.3 s, 2.17.0 @14.8 s, high @44.2 s) and not in the landing arm at max; on the pass it fired early and everything downstream was a short call. Making the copy unconditional (or moving it to the CLI boundary, issue #213) is the lever that would remove the remaining non-determinism.
best-agent issue #213 remains orthogonal and still real: gcode was boundary-stopped in both arms.
